newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA WANTS TO TIER ONE AT ABOUT SEVEN PCT.
newsitem.headline: CBA WANTS TO TIER ONE AT ABOUT SEVEN PCT.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Wednesday that over the longer term it would like its tier one capital ratio to be about seven percent.
"We would like that to hover around the seven percent mark," CBA managing director David Murray told reporters.
CBA's tier one ratio stood at 8.6 percent at the end of June this year but this is expected to fall to 7.9 percent once a A$650 million share buyback is completed.
Murray said he was not able to predict whether CBA had excess capital for more buybacks because it had a high dividend payout ratio and was planning significant new investments.
He said however that the most accurate measure of tier one capital for CBA excluded about A$1 billion in government guaranteed tier one notes.
This adjusted measure would fall to about 7.4 percent once the buy-back had been completed, a CBA spokeswoman said Later.
"That would fit nicely in the bank's target of about 7.0 to 7.5 percent," she said.
The notes are scheduled to slowly move out of tier one over the next two years as they mature or are refinanced into less highly rated assets.
